title: Mountain Biking in India: Trails, Routes and Seasons
seoTitle: Mountain Biking in India: Trails, Routes & Seasons | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Mountain biking in India: Manali to Leh, the Khardung La descent, Spiti, the Western Ghats and trails near Bengaluru and Pune, with seasons, bike hire and safety.
description: A guide to mountain biking and cycle touring in India: the Manali to Leh highway, the Khardung La downhill, Spiti and Kinnaur, forest and estate trails in Coorg and Chikmagalur, the Sahyadris near Pune, and how to plan, hire bikes and ride safely.
dek: From supported rides over 5,000-metre passes to single-track in the Western Ghats, India has cycling adventures for every level. Here is where to ride.

hero.caption: Mountain roads in Ladakh

intro: Mountain biking in India ranges from multi-day, vehicle-supported rides across the high passes of Ladakh and Spiti to half-day trail rides through coffee estates and forests in the Western Ghats. Cycling clubs in cities such as Bengaluru, Pune and Mumbai organise regular weekend trail rides, and several operators run guided tours with rental bikes and support vehicles.

This guide covers the classic long-distance routes, shorter trail areas, when to ride and what to arrange. It is written for fit cyclists; the Himalayan routes in particular need training and acclimatisation.
quickAnswer: The best places for mountain biking in India are the Manali to Leh highway and Leh's Khardung La descent (about July to September), the Spiti and Kinnaur circuit, and forest and plantation trails in Coorg, Chikmagalur and the Sahyadris near Pune in the dry months. Beginners can start with a guided downhill ride from Khardung La or a half-day estate ride. Long Himalayan rides need training, acclimatisation and a support vehicle.
takeaways: Manali to Leh by bicycle takes most riders 8 to 12 days with acclimatisation.
A guided downhill ride from Khardung La to Leh is a popular half-day taste of Himalayan biking.
The Western Ghats are ridden from about October to February; trails are muddy and leech-filled in the monsoon.
Guided tours usually include bike rental, a support vehicle and a mechanic.
Carry spares; bike shops are rare outside big towns and Leh.

items.name: Manali to Leh
body: One of the great cycle tours: roughly 430 km from Manali to Leh via the Atal Tunnel, Keylong, Baralacha La, the More Plains and Tanglang La at over 5,000 metres. Most riders take eight to twelve days, with rest days for acclimatisation, and use a support vehicle for water, food and camping gear.

items.name: Khardung La to Leh downhill
body: Operators in Leh drive riders and bikes up to Khardung La and let them ride the long descent back to Leh on the paved road. It needs confidence on a bike and good brakes more than fitness.

items.name: Spiti and Kinnaur
body: Riding the Spiti circuit by bicycle takes around two weeks, with rough roads over Kunzum Pass and long climbs out of the Sutlej valley. Shorter rides from Kaza to villages such as Langza, Komic and Kibber are good day trips.

items.name: Kullu and Manali valleys
body: Forest roads and village trails around Manali, Naggar and the Kullu valley suit day rides, and rental shops in Manali hire mountain bikes.

facts.Season: April to June, September to November

items.name: Garhwal and Kumaon, Uttarakhand
body: Hill roads between towns such as Mussoorie, Dhanaulti and Kanatal, or around Nainital and Mukteshwar, make good road and gravel rides with steady climbs.

items.name: Coorg and Chikmagalur, Karnataka
body: Estate roads and forest tracks through coffee plantations, with steep climbs and fast descents. Some routes cross private estates, so ride with a local guide or club.

items.name: Sahyadris near Pune and Lonavala
body: Trails and farm roads around Sinhagad, the Pawna lake area and the plateaus near Lonavala are ridden by Pune's cycling community. Expect rocky, technical sections.

items.name: Around Bengaluru
body: Weekend riders head to trails near Ramanagara, Nandi Hills and the forests on the city's edge. Cycling clubs run group rides.

items.name: Munnar and the Kerala hills
body: Tea estate roads around Munnar offer climbs and views; ride early before traffic.

sections.heading: Types of riding
paras: Cycling adventures in India fall into three broad kinds. Long-distance touring on paved and broken mountain roads, such as Manali to Leh, needs endurance more than technical skill. Trail riding on forest and estate tracks, as in Coorg or the Sahyadris, needs bike handling on rocks, roots and mud. Downhill rides, such as the descent from Khardung La, are mostly about braking and line choice.

Pick a trip that matches the riding you enjoy and have trained for. A strong road cyclist may find rocky single-track harder than expected, and a trail rider may struggle with a week of climbing above 4,000 metres.

sections.heading: Planning a cycling trip
list: Decide between self-supported touring and a guided tour with a support vehicle; the latter is far easier at high altitude.
Hire bikes in Manali or Leh, or bring your own in a bike box by train or flight.
Train with long rides and hill repeats for at least two months before a Himalayan tour.
Carry spare tubes, a pump, chain tool, brake pads, derailleur hanger and multi-tool.
Plan water and food stops; villages are far apart on high routes.
Wear a helmet, gloves and bright clothing; share the road carefully with trucks and army convoys.

safety: On Himalayan routes, gain height gradually, sleep lower where possible and descend if altitude sickness symptoms worsen.
Wear a helmet on every ride, including downhills.
Check brakes before every descent; long Himalayan descents overheat brake pads.
Avoid riding after dark and in heavy traffic on highways.
Carry at least two litres of water and electrolytes; the air is dry at altitude.
In the Western Ghats, watch for wildlife and follow forest department rules on closed roads.

faqs.q: Where can I go mountain biking in India?
faqs.a: Ladakh, Spiti and the Kullu valley in the Himalaya, and Coorg, Chikmagalur, the Sahyadris and the hills around Bengaluru in the south and west.

faqs.q: How long does it take to cycle from Manali to Leh?
faqs.a: Most riders take eight to twelve days, including acclimatisation.

faqs.q: Can beginners go mountain biking in Ladakh?
faqs.a: The guided Khardung La to Leh downhill suits confident beginners. Long rides over the passes need experience and training.

faqs.q: When is the best time for cycling in the Western Ghats?
faqs.a: From about October to February, after the monsoon and before the summer heat.

faqs.q: Can I rent a mountain bike in Manali or Leh?
faqs.a: Yes, rental shops and tour operators in both towns hire mountain bikes, often with helmets and basic tools.
